1669-the-human-drift.title: The Human Drift
1669-the-human-drift.creator: Jack London
1669-the-human-drift.description: A book by Jack London. There have been drifts from east to west and west to east, from north to south and back again, drifts that have criss-crossed one another, and drifts colliding and recoiling and caroming off in new directions. From Central Europe the Aryans have drifted into Asia, and from Central Asia the Turanians have drifted across Europe.

23469-a-history-of-the-four-georges-volu.title: A History Of The Four Georges
23469-a-history-of-the-four-georges-volu.creator: Justin Mccarthy, M.P.
23469-a-history-of-the-four-georges-volu.description: A book by Justin Mccarthy, M.P.. "The Queen is pretty well," Swift wrote to Lord Peterborough on May 18, 1714, "at present, but the least disorder she has puts all in alarm." Swift goes on to tell his correspondent that "when it is over we act as if she were immortal; neither is it possible to persuade people to make any preparations against an evil day."  Yet on the condition of Queen Anne's health depended to all appearance the continuance of peace in England.

arxiv-2212-10983.title: Computer says “No”: The Case Against Empathetic Conversational AI
arxiv-2212-10983.creator: Alba Curry, Amanda Cercas Curry
arxiv-2212-10983.description: Abstract Emotions are an integral part of human cognition and they guide not only our understanding of the world but also our actions within it. As such, whether we soothe or flame an emotion is not inconsequential. Recent work in conversational AI has focused on responding empathetically to users, validating and soothing their emotions without a real basis.

arxiv-2402-06783.title: Learn to Teach: Sample-Efficient Privileged Learning for Humanoid Locomotion over Diverse Terrains
arxiv-2402-06783.creator: Feiyang Wu, Xavier Nal, Jaehwi Jang, Wei Zhu, Zhaoyuan Gu, Anqi Wu, Ye Zhao
arxiv-2402-06783.description: Abstract Humanoid robots promise transformative capabilities for industrial and service applications. While recent advances in Reinforcement Learning (RL) yield impressive results in locomotion, manipulation, and navigation, the proposed methods typically require enormous simulation samples to account for real-world variability. This work proposes a novel one-stage training framework—Learn to Teach (L2T)—which unifies teacher and student policy learning.

arxiv-2405-07264.title: Information Rates Over Multi-View Channels
arxiv-2405-07264.creator: V. Arvind Rameshwar and Nir Weinberger
arxiv-2405-07264.description: Abstract We investigate the fundamental limits of reliable communication over multi-view channels, in which the channel output is comprised of a large number of independent noisy views of a transmitted symbol. We consider first the setting of multi-view discrete memoryless channels and then extend our results to general multi-view channels (using multi-letter formulas).

arxiv-2409-09002.title: Enigmatic 2+6/13 Filling Factor: A Prototype Intermittent Topological State
arxiv-2409-09002.creator: Sudipto Das, Sahana Das, Sudhansu S. Mandal
arxiv-2409-09002.description: Abstract Observation of filling factor 6/13 is one of the surprising fractional quantum Hall states in the second Landau level because, in contrast to the standard wisdom, the fractions ( ν < 1 / 2 \nu<1/2 ) with lower numerators, namely 4 and 5, have not yet been observed.

pmc-10576284.creator: Hanan Boodai, Mohamed ElSalhy, Aishah Alsumait, Jitendra Ariga, Marwan Al-Sharbati
pmc-10576284.description: BackgroundUnderstanding oral health behaviour s and their impact on Oral Health-Related Quality of Life (OHRQoL) may serve as an instrument to articulate the conventional oral health policy framework, thereby ameliorating the overall health of young individuals in the long term.

pmc-10657806.title: Exploring the origins of decreased sound tolerance in tinnitus patients
pmc-10657806.creator: Eun Hye Kim, Seung-Ho Shin, Sung Wan Byun, Ho Yun Lee
pmc-10657806.description: This study aimed to confirm the characteristics of auditory function alterations in tinnitus patients with concomitant decreased sound tolerance (ST) and provide insights for developing tailored therapeutic approaches. A retrospective analysis was conducted on patient records from a tertiary university hospital's tinnitus clinic between March 2020 and June 2023. Demographic attributes and audiological profiles were reviewed.

pmc-11432831.title: Efficient lung cancer detection using computational intelligence and ensemble learning
pmc-11432831.creator: Richa Jain, Parminder Singh, Mohamed Abdelkader, Wadii Boulila
pmc-11432831.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Lung cancer emerges as a major factor in cancer-related fatalities in the current generation, and it is predicted to continue having a long-term impact. Detecting symptoms early becomes crucial for effective treatment, underscoring innovative therapy’s necessity. Many researchers have conducted extensive work in this area, yet challenges such as high false-positive rates and achieving high accuracy in detection continue to complicate accurate diagnosis.

pmc-12469344.title: Molecular Screening for Cervical Cancer
pmc-12469344.creator: Toni Ricardo Martins, José Eduardo Levi, Emiliano Giardina, Gustavo Barra
pmc-12469344.description: Background/Objectives: Cervical cancer (CC), a highly prevalent female neoplasia, has been prevented through repeated cervicovaginal cytology, the so-called Pap test, across women’s lifespans. The now undebatable role of Human Papillomaviruses in the etiology of CC and the development of high-throughput automated molecular amplification diagnostic platforms is allowing for the replacement of the Pap test with HPV testing.

pmc-12502519.title: Single-cell in situ mapping of glioblastoma and astrocyte cell lines treated with a carbon dot–mediated riluzole nanotherapeutic agent: a live-cell µFTIR and soft X-ray tomography approach
pmc-12502519.creator: Tanja Dučić, Eva Pereiro, Milena Ninkovic, Swetlana Sperling, Veit Rohde, Claudia Fernández-González, Manuel Algarra, Elena González-Muñoz
pmc-12502519.description: Nanoparticle-based drug carriers offer a promising alternative to conventional cancer therapies by enabling targeted delivery and reducing off-target toxicity. Here, we used synthesised and characterised carbon-based nanoparticles derived from 2-acrylamido-2-methylpropanesulfonic acid (AMPS-CDs), demonstrating biocompatibility with both human astrocytes and glioblastoma cells.

pmc-12532695.title: Plasma proteomic associations with Alzheimer’s disease endophenotypes
pmc-12532695.creator: Shiva Afshar, Eric B. Dammer, Shijia Bian, David A. Bennett, Richard Mohs, Doug Beauregard, John Dwyer, Chadwick M. Hales, Felicia C. Goldstein, Monica W. Parker, Antoine R. Trammell, Caroline M. Watson, Todd E. Golde, Nicholas T. Seyfried, Blaine R. Roberts, Cecelia M. Manzanares, James J. Lah, All
pmc-12532695.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Clinical Alzheimer’s disease is currently characterized by cerebral β-amyloidosis associated with cognitive impairment. However, most cases of Alzheimer’s disease are associated with multiple neuropathologies at autopsy. The peripheral protein changes associated with these disease endophenotypes are poorly understood.

pmc-12622963.title: Deep learning-based classification of colorectal cancer in histopathology images for category detection
pmc-12622963.creator: Thang Truong Le, Vinh-Thuyen Nguyen-Truong, Quang Van Nhat Duong, Nghia Trong Le Phan, Phuc Nguyen Thien Dao, Mqondisi Fortune Mavuso, Huy Ngoc Anh Nguyen, Tien Thuy Mai, Kiep Thi Quang
pmc-12622963.description: Accurate and timely diagnosis of colorectal cancer (CRC) is essential for effective treatment and better patient outcomes. This study explores the application of deep learning (DL) for automated CRC categories classification using hematoxylin and eosin-stained histopathology (H&E) images. Among the models, ResNet-34 demonstrated a strong balance of performance and complexity, achieving an overall accuracy of 85.

pmc-13167450.title: Physical understanding of the extreme global temperature jump in 2023
pmc-13167450.creator: J. Mex, C. Cassou, A. Jézéquel, S. Bony, C. Deser
pmc-13167450.description: Global surface air temperature reached unprecedented heights in early boreal fall 2023, surpassing the previous record for year-to-year temperature increase by a significant margin. We attribute most of this temperature jump to the onset and maturing stages of the 2023 El Niño, with some contributions from the North Atlantic.

pmc-13635496.title: Selective percutaneous myofasciotomy in persistent toe-walking: Anatomical rationale and surgical technique
pmc-13635496.creator: David Pomarino, Alexander Yakovlevich Nazarkin, Amel Sidi Athmane, Anna Ryzhanok, Bastian Fregien, Kevin M Rostásy
pmc-13635496.description: Persistent toe-walking is a gait abnormality characterized by forefoot initial contact and reduced or absent heel strike beyond early childhood. Although often regarded as a transient developmental variant, persistence of this pattern may lead to progressive limitation of ankle dorsiflexion, fixed equinus contracture, and long-term functional impairment.

pmc-13653706.title: Central Obesity Disrupts Brain Network Organization in Aging via Metabolic and Structural Pathways
pmc-13653706.creator: Marina Fernandez-Alvarez, Karel M. Lopez-Vilaret, Jose L. Cantero, Mercedes Atienza
pmc-13653706.description: Obesity is a recognized risk factor for age-related cognitive decline, with central (abdominal) obesity posing a particular strong threat to brain health. In a cross-sectional study of 89 cognitively healthy adults (52-79 years, mean 65.7 ± 6.4; 58 women), we compared the effects of central versus overall obesity on brain connectivity measured with resting-state fMRI.
